q: Under PD 1096, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies without a sprinkler system?
n: 45 m unsprinklered, stretching to 60 m once sprinklers are installed.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum exit door width applies?
n: 800 mm, narrower than the 900 mm PD 1096 requires.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to an institutional sleeping department?
n: 11.00 sq m per person for sleeping, against 22.00 sq m for in-patient treatment.

q: In a PD 957 project with 1000 or more occupants, how many exits are required?
n: Four. PD 957 follows the PD 1096 counts: one below 10, two to 499, three to 999, four beyond.

q: Under the Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applies to an institutional sleeping area?
n: 11.10 sq m per person, a hair looser than the 11.00 sq m PD 1096 uses. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to warehouses?
n: Warehouses are 46.50 sq m per person, the loosest factor in the Code, together with aircraft hangars.

q: In an open market development, what minimum level of completion applies to a single-detached unit?
o: Complete House based on submitted specifications
Shell House based on submitted specifications
n: A complete house, built to the submitted specifications. Only socialized housing may be handed over as a shell.

q: Under RA 9514, how many exits must a balcony, mezzanine or storey have for more than 500 and up to 1000 occupants?
n: Three, rising to four above 1000.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must a socialized-housing duplex or single-attached lot have?
n: 6.00 m, against 8.00 m in an open market subdivision.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum headroom must a sidewalk or walkway have?
n: 2.20 m, that is 2200 mm. Anything hanging below 2.00 m must be guarded so a person with a visual disability does not walk into it.

q: In an open market subdivision under PD 957, what maximum passageway slope applies?
n: 1:8, the same limit PD 1096 sets for an exit passageway.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies with a sprinkler system?
n: 61 m with sprinklers, 46 m without.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum height may a threshold have?
n: 130 mm. Anything higher stops being a threshold and becomes a step.

q: What minimum exit width must a stage have?
n: 900 mm for the stage exit itself, with a 750 mm exit stair.

q: Under BP 220, what maximum dead-end length applies?
n: 12.00 m, twice the 6.00 m PD 1096 allows.

q: Under PD 1096, what maximum block length applies to row houses?
n: 100 m, with at most 20 units in that block.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum corridor width applies?
n: 1.10 m. BP 220 and BP 344 both ask a little more at 1.20 m.

q: In a PD 957 project with 500 to 999 occupants, how many exits are required?
n: Three. It steps to four at 1000 occupants.

q: Under BP 220, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies without a sprinkler system?
n: 45 m, the same figure PD 1096 uses.

q: Under PD 1096, when must a mezzanine have two stairways?
o: When it exceeds 185.00 sq. m or 18.00 m in any dimension
When it exceeds 250.00 sq. m or 20.00 m
When it exceeds 50.00 sq. m or 10.00 m
When it exceeds 100.00 sq. m or 12.00 m
n: Once it exceeds 185.00 sq m, or 18.00 m in any one direction. Either trigger is enough.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to a mercantile ground floor with direct street access?
n: 2.80 sq m per person on the ground floor and in the basement, 5.60 sq m on upper floors. Street level draws the densest crowd.

q: Under PD 1096, what maximum dead-end length applies to a corridor?
n: 6.00 m. Past that an occupant could walk away from the only exit.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum depth must a pedestrian median or island at a crossing have?
n: At least 1500 mm deep, preferably 2000 mm, so a wheelchair can wait clear of traffic.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width must the opening from a sleeping room to the outside have?
n: 90 cm from a sleeping room to the outside, against 60 cm for an interior door.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum floor area and least dimension must a room for human habitation have?
n: 6.00 sq m with a least dimension of 2.00 m. A long thin 6 sq m room does not qualify.

q: A habitable room relies on natural ventilation. What minimum ceiling height applies?
n: 2.70 m with natural ventilation, against 2.40 m where the room is mechanically ventilated.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear height must be kept above an accessible parking space?
n: 2200 mm from the parking floor, so a van with a roof-mounted lift can enter.

q: What minimum exit door height applies across the building laws?
n: 2.00 m. Only the widths differ: 900 mm under PD 1096, 800 mm under BP 220.

q: In an open market subdivision under PD 957, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies with sprinklers?
n: 60 m with sprinklers, 45 m without, following the PD 1096 figures.

q: Under PD 1096, how many exits are required for an occupant load of 10 to 499?
n: Two. Above the first storey, any occupant load over 10 already needs two.

q: Under the Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applies to reviewing stands, stadia and waiting spaces?
n: 0.28 sq m per person, far denser than the 0.65 sq m PD 1096 assigns. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: When is a sleeping room excused from having an outside window for escape?
o: It is omitted if the room has one door
It is not required if the room has two doors
It is required only above the second floor
It is optional for corner rooms
n: When the room already has two doors. Two ways out make the window unnecessary.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to a dry nursery with sleeping?
n: 3.30 sq m per person, close to the 3.25 sq m PD 1096 gives a children’s nursery.

q: Under BP 220, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies with a sprinkler system?
n: 60 m with sprinklers, against 45 m without.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must an irregular single-detached lot have?
n: 10.00 m, just under the 12.00 m required of a corner lot.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to hospitals and sanitaria?
n: 8.40 sq m per person. Nursing homes and homes for the aged are looser at 7.40 sq m.

q: In a PD 957 project with 10 to 499 occupants, how many exits are required?
n: Two, following the PD 1096 counts.

q: Under PD 1096, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies with a sprinkler system?
n: 60 m. Sprinklers buy 15 m over the 45 m allowed without them.

q: A sprinklered project is built under BP 220. What maximum travel distance to an exit applies?
n: 60 m. Without sprinklers it drops to 45 m.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum size must an accessible toilet cubicle have?
n: At least 1800 by 1800 mm, that is 3.24 sq m. The 1994 IRR required only 1.70 by 1.80 m.

q: How many exits must a boiler room have?
n: Two. A boiler room is where fire starts, so no occupant may be cornered in it.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must a socialized-housing single-detached corner lot have?
n: 8.00 m, two thirds of the 12.00 m an open market corner lot needs.

q: Under PD 1096, how many exits are required for an occupant load of 500 to 999?
n: Three. Four are required at 1000 or more.

q: How high above the floor may the outside window of a sleeping room sit?
n: 1.22 m above the floor, about chest height, so an adult can climb through it.

q: For an interior lot with E, F, G, H or I occupancy, what minimum open space applies?
n: 20%, against 50% for A, B, C, D and J occupancies on the same lot.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must a single-detached corner lot have?
n: 12.00 m, the widest frontage in the schedule. A corner lot must address two streets.

q: Under BP 220, what residential open space applies to an interior lot?
n: 50% for residential use, 25% for anything else.

q: Under PD 957, what minimum area must a studio unit have?
n: 18 sq m, three times the 6.00 sq m PD 1096 sets for a single habitable room.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applied to grouped industrial uses?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 9.30 sq m per person, the same figure used for offices. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to a mercantile basement?
n: 2.80 sq m per person, the same as the ground floor. Upper floors ease to 5.60 sq m.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to nursing homes, children’s homes and homes for the aged?
n: 7.40 sq m per person, looser than the 8.40 sq m used for hospitals.

q: Under PD 1096, how many exits are required for an occupant load of 1000 or more?
n: Four, the highest count the Code requires.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to an end lot with A, B, C, D, E2 or H occupancy?
n: 30% to 50%. An end lot has one boundary free, so it falls between an interior and a corner lot.

q: How many exits must the stage itself have?
n: One exit at 900 mm wide, plus a 750 mm exit stair.

q: Under BP 220 and BP 344, what minimum corridor width applies?
n: 1.20 m for both, against 1.10 m under PD 1096.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to grouped industrial uses?
n: 9.30 sq m per person, unchanged from the 1977 Fire Code.

q: A required window must be sheltered by an eave. What minimum horizontal projection must the eave have?
n: At least 750 mm over the window, enough to keep rain out while the window stays open.

q: Which law sets the 2.70 m minimum ceiling height for a naturally ventilated habitable room?
n: Ceiling heights come from PD 1096: 2.40 m with artificial ventilation, 2.70 m with natural. BP 344 governs accessibility and sets no ceiling height.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what minimum number of exits applied whatever the occupant load?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: At least two. PD 1096 is gentler, allowing one below 10 occupants. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under PD 1096, how many exits are required for an occupant load below 10?
n: One. It becomes two once the load passes 10 on any floor above the first.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to an in-patient institutional treatment department?
n: 22.00 sq m per person for treatment, twice the 11.00 sq m used for sleeping.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to non-residential uses on a corner lot?
n: 15% for other uses, against 10% for residential.

q: A stand sits 0.50 m above ground level and holds more than 50 persons. How many exits does it need?
n: Two, and it must be open at both ends.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to conference rooms, exhibit rooms and gymnasia?
n: 1.40 sq m per person. Classrooms are tighter still at 1.80 sq m.

q: What minimum width must a stage exit stair have?
n: 750 mm, narrower than the 900 mm stage exit itself.

q: A mercantile upper floor is assessed under PD 1096. What floor area per person applies?
n: 5.60 sq m per person upstairs, against 2.80 sq m on the ground floor.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum travel distance to an exit applied with a sprinkler system?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 61 m with sprinklers, 46 m without. RA 9514 carries the same two figures. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under BP 220, what level of completion applies to socialized duplex, single-attached and row house units?
o: Shell House based on submitted specifications
Complete House based on submitted specifications
n: A shell house built to the submitted specifications, which the buyer finishes.

q: How must a stand holding more than 50 persons be arranged?
n: Open at both ends, with two exits, so the crowd can clear either way.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to non-residential uses on a corner-through lot?
n: 15%, the same as any other non-residential corner condition.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to aircraft hangars with no repair work?
n: 46.50 sq m per person, the same as warehouses. Parking garages are 18.60 and ordinary garages 9.30.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, what minimum clear door width is required?
n: All doors must give at least 900 mm clear. The 1994 IRR required only 800 mm.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to non-residential uses on a through lot?
n: 15%, against 10% for residential.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum clear height applies to the storeys above the second?
n: 2.10 m of unobstructed headroom. The first storey needs 2.70 m and the second 2.40 m.

q: In a dwelling with more than two rooms, what may one of the two required exits be?
o: One may be a door or stairway
n: A door or a stairway. Only one of the two has to be a full exit.

q: Under RA 9514, how many exits must a balcony, mezzanine or storey have above 1000 occupants?
n: Four, the top of the scale.

q: Under PD 1096, how many row house units may a single block hold?
n: 20 units per block, within a 100 m block length.

q: What minimum width must a passageway from an inner court have?
n: At least 1.20 m, so the court is not a trap.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum level of completion applies to a socialized single-detached unit?
o: Shell House based on submitted specifications
Complete House based on submitted specifications
n: A shell house to the submitted specifications. Economic housing must be handed over complete.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to mercantile upper floors?
n: 5.60 sq m per person, double the 2.80 sq m used at street level.

q: Under BP 220, what standard governs the open space on an end lot?
n: PD 1096. BP 220 sets its own figures for the other lot types but defers on end lots.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must an interior socialized-housing single-detached lot have?
n: 3.00 m, the narrowest frontage allowed, since an interior lot reaches the street through an access strip.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to offices, storage and shipping?
n: 9.30 sq m per person, matching PD 1096. The 1977 Fire Code was denser at 5.60 sq m.

q: Under RA 9514, what illumination must an exit sign receive?
n: 0.005 lumens per square centimetre, the same value the 1977 Fire Code used.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum dead-end length applies to a corridor?
n: 6.00 m, matching PD 1096.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to a nursery for children?
n: 3.25 sq m per person, the densest institutional figure.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must an interior single-detached lot have?
n: 3.00 m, the same as socialized housing. An interior lot needs only an access strip.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to auditoriums, theaters, churches and dance floors?
n: 0.65 sq m per person, the densest in the Code. Assembly spaces pack people standing or seated.

q: Under the 2024 Revised IRR of BP 344, how far apart may rest stops be along a long accessible walkway?
n: At most 12000 mm between rest stops, so a wheelchair user or a person with a cane can pause.

q: A treatment area is assessed under RA 9514. What occupant-load factor applies?
n: 22.30 sq m per person, against 22.00 sq m under PD 1096.

q: How many exits must an open-air stand holding more than 300 persons have?
n: Two. Indoors the same rule bites at 50 persons, because smoke has nowhere to go.

q: Under PD 1096, what maximum slope may an exit passageway have?
n: 1:8. An exit court is held flatter, at 1:10.

q: Under the Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applies to an institutional treatment area?
n: 22.30 sq m per person, just above the 22.00 sq m PD 1096 uses. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: In an open market subdivision under PD 957, what maximum dead-end length applies?
n: 12.00 m, the same allowance BP 220 gives.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must a socialized-housing row house have?
n: 3.50 m, against 4.00 m for economic and open market row houses.

q: A classroom is assessed under RA 9514. What floor area per person applies?
n: 1.90 sq m per person, marginally looser than the 1.80 sq m PD 1096 uses.

q: Under BP 220, what residential open space applies to an inside lot?
n: 20% residential, 15% for other uses.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to an interior lot with A, B, C, D or J occupancy?
n: 50%. An interior lot is hemmed in on every side, so it must give up the most.

q: RA 9514 sets no room ceiling height. What clear height does it require along a means of egress?
n: The 2019 Revised IRR requires 2.00 m of headroom along a means of egress, and no ceiling projection lower than 2.00 m. Room ceiling heights are a PD 1096 matter.

q: For an inside lot with E, F, G, H or I occupancy, what minimum open space applies?
n: 15%, against 20% for A, B, C, D and J occupancies.

q: Under PD 1096, what clear height must a mezzanine have above and below it?
n: 1.80 m above and below. It is the one ceiling figure BP 220 matches exactly.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to offices, storage and shipping?
n: 9.30 sq m per person, the same figure ordinary garages take.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to non-residential uses on an interior lot?
n: 25%, half the 50% required of residential use on the same lot.

q: In an open market development under PD 957, what minimum court dimension applies?
n: 1.50 m, tighter than the 2.00 m PD 1096 sets.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum ceiling height applies to the first storey of a multi-storey building?
n: 2.70 m at the first storey, 2.40 m at the second, 2.10 m of headroom above that.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what maximum travel distance to an exit applied without a sprinkler system?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 46 m unsprinklered, 61 m sprinklered. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what illumination did an exit sign require?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 0.005 lumens per square centimetre, carried forward unchanged into RA 9514. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under BP 220, what maximum block length applies in economic and socialized housing?
n: 400 m, with a 2.0 m alley at midlength once the block passes 250 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to garages?
n: 9.30 sq m per person for an ordinary garage. A parking garage is looser at 18.60 sq m.

q: For an inside lot with A, B, C, D or J occupancy, what minimum open space applies?
n: 20%. An inside lot fronts a street, so it needs less than the 50% of an interior lot.

q: What minimum window opening must a room have, as a fraction of its floor area?
o: At least 10% of the floor area
n: At least 10% of the floor area, with half of that openable for ventilation.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum ceiling height applies to a habitable room with artificial ventilation?
n: 2.40 m with artificial ventilation. Rely on natural ventilation and it rises to 2.70 m.

q: How far must eaves project over a required window?
n: At least 750 mm.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applied to residential occupancy?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 18.00 sq m per person, far denser than the 28.00 sq m PD 1096 assigns a dwelling. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum corridor width applies?
n: 1.12 m, between the 1.10 m of PD 1096 and the 1.20 m of BP 220.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum ceiling height applies to a habitable room in economic or socialized housing?
n: BP 220 uses one figure, 2.00 m, whatever the ventilation. PD 1096 is the law that splits it into 2.40 m and 2.70 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a corner lot with A, B, C, D or J occupancy?
n: 10%. Two street frontages already give the lot light and air.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to classrooms?
n: 1.80 sq m per person. Conference rooms and gymnasia are denser still at 1.40 sq m.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must a regular single-detached lot have?
n: 6.00 m. A corner lot needs twice that at 12.00 m.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum width must a means of egress have?
n: 710 mm minimum, 1220 mm maximum for a single unit of exit width.

q: In an open market subdivision under PD 957, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies without sprinklers?
n: 45 m, rising to 60 m with sprinklers.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum clear height must a mezzanine have?
n: 1.80 m, the same figure PD 1096 uses, while BP 220 rooms themselves need only 2.00 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to mechanical equipment rooms?
n: 28.00 sq m per person, the same as a dwelling. Few people, spread thin.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum ceiling height applies to the second storey?
n: 2.40 m at the second storey, below the 2.70 m required at the first.

q: How far above the roof must a firewall extend for the required clearance?
n: 1.00 m above the roof, so fire cannot lap over it.

q: What least dimension must the outside window of a sleeping room have?
n: 56 cm, with an area of at least 0.45 sq m.

q: Which law splits its minimum ceiling height by ventilation, 2.40 m artificial and 2.70 m natural?
n: Only PD 1096 splits the figure. BP 220 sets a flat 2.00 m, and neither RA 9514 nor BP 344 sets a room ceiling height at all.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum mezzanine height applies in economic and socialized housing?
n: 1.80 m, against the 2.00 m required of an ordinary room.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a through lot with A, B, C, D or J occupancy?
n: 10%, the same as a corner lot. Both have two open sides.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a corner-through lot, whatever the occupancy?
n: 5%, the lowest requirement, because three sides already open onto streets.

q: Under BP 220, what residential open space applies to a corner-through lot?
n: 10% residential, 15% for other uses.

q: How many exits must a dwelling with more than two rooms have?
n: Two, one of which may be a door or a stairway.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum area and least dimension must a kitchen have?
n: 3.00 sq m with a least dimension of 1.50 m, half the area required of a habitable room.

q: In an open market development, what maximum block length applies to row houses?
n: 400 m, four times the 100 m PD 1096 allows.

q: In an open market development, what level of completion applies to duplex, single-attached and row house units?
o: Shell House based on submitted specifications
Complete House based on submitted specifications
n: A complete house, built to the submitted specifications.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum travel distance to an exit applies without a sprinkler system?
n: 46 m without sprinklers, 61 m with them. PD 1096 is a metre tighter at 45 m and 60 m.

q: Under BP 220, what limit applies to the sum of opening areas in any storey?
n: Less than 25% of the wall area on that storey, half of what PD 1096 allows.

q: Under RA 9514, how many exits must a balcony, mezzanine or storey have for 100 to 500 occupants?
n: Two. It steps to three above 500 and four above 1000.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must a duplex or single-attached lot have?
n: 8.00 m, against 6.00 m in socialized housing.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to classrooms?
n: 1.90 sq m per person, against 1.80 sq m under PD 1096.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to mercantile upper floors?
n: 5.60 sq m per person, matching PD 1096.

q: In an open market development under PD 957, what limit applies to the sum of opening areas in a storey?
n: Less than 50% of the wall area on that storey, following PD 1096.

q: Under PD 1096, what limit applies to the sum of opening areas in any storey?
n: Less than 50% of the wall area on that storey. Past half, the wall stops being a wall.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applied to a mercantile ground floor with direct access?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 4.30 sq m per person, looser than the 2.80 sq m PD 1096 and RA 9514 both use. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under BP 220, what residential open space applies to a corner lot?
n: 10% residential, 15% for other uses.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to a split-level mercantile space?
n: 3.70 sq m per person, between the 2.80 sq m ground floor and the 5.60 sq m upper floors.

q: Under the 1977 Fire Code, what occupant-load factor applied to offices, storage and shipping?
ref: PD 1185, the 1977 Fire Code (repealed by RA 9514)
n: 5.60 sq m per person, far denser than the 9.30 sq m used today. RA 9514 replaced PD 1185 in 2008.

q: Under the 2019 Revised IRR of RA 9514, what minimum ceiling height applies to a fire command center?
n: A fire command center needs 2.40 m of ceiling height, at least 10.00 sq m of floor area, and no dimension under 1.50 m.

q: A project is built under BP 220. What minimum exit door height applies?
n: 2.00 m, the same height every one of these laws requires.

q: Under the 2019 Revised IRR of RA 9514, what is the minimum floor area of a fire command center?
n: 10.00 sq m minimum, separated by two-hour fire-resistive construction, with a 2.40 m ceiling.

q: Under RA 9514, what maximum width applies to a single unit of exit width?
n: 1220 mm maximum, 710 mm minimum.

q: What occupant-load factor applies to dining rooms, drinking establishments, exhibit rooms and gymnasia?
n: 1.40 sq m per person.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to non-residential uses on an inside lot?
n: 15%, against 20% for residential.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a through lot with E, F, G, H or I occupancy?
n: 5%, half the 10% required of A, B, C, D and J occupancies.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must an irregular socialized-housing single-detached lot have?
n: 8.00 m, the same as a socialized-housing corner lot.

q: In a medium cost development, what minimum frontage must a row house have?
n: 4.00 m, the same as the open market figure. Only socialized housing drops to 3.50 m.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to parking garages?
n: 18.60 sq m per person for a parking garage, against 9.30 sq m for an ordinary garage.

q: Under PD 1096, what illumination must an exit sign receive?
n: 10.7 lux at floor level.

q: In an open market subdivision under PD 957, what minimum exit door width applies?
n: 900 mm, following PD 1096. BP 220 housing may drop to 800 mm.

q: In an open market development, what must be provided at midlength when a row house block exceeds 250 m?
n: A 2.0 m alley at midlength, so residents are not forced to walk the full block.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum dimension must a court have?
n: 2.00 m for a one or two storey building, with a 1.20 m passageway out of an inner court.

q: Under RA 9514, what minimum exit door width applies?
n: 710 mm, the narrowest of the laws. PD 1096 requires 900 mm.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum frontage must a regular socialized-housing single-detached lot have?
n: 4.00 m, against 6.00 m in an open market subdivision.

q: In an open market development, what minimum frontage must a row house have?
n: 4.00 m, narrowing to 3.50 m in socialized housing.

q: Under BP 220, what minimum width must an interior door have?
n: 60 cm for an interior door, against 90 cm from a sleeping room to the outside.

q: What minimum headroom clearance applies across these building laws?
n: 2.00 m, the one figure PD 1096, BP 220 and the Fire Code all agree on.

q: What occupant-load factor applies to shops and laboratories?
n: 4.60 sq m per person, the same under PD 1096 and both fire codes.

q: Under BP 220, how many exits are required in economic or socialized housing for an occupant load below 10?
n: One, the same as PD 1096. Two are required at 10 or more.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to an end lot with H1, H2, H4 or E3 occupancy?
n: 5%. The same lot with A, B, C, D, E2 or H occupancy needs 30% to 50%.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a corner lot abutting three or more streets or rivers?
n: 5%, the floor of the scale, since the lot is almost entirely edged by open space already.

q: How many exits must a dressing room have?
n: Two, each 750 mm wide.

q: Under RA 9514, what occupant-load factor applies to a mercantile ground floor with direct access?
n: 2.80 sq m per person, the same as PD 1096. The 1977 Fire Code was looser at 4.30 sq m.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to a dwelling?
n: 28.00 sq m per person, the loosest residential figure. The 1977 Fire Code assumed 18.00 sq m.

q: Under the 2019 Revised IRR of RA 9514, what least dimension must a fire command center have?
n: No dimension under 1.50 m, with at least 10.00 sq m of area and a 2.40 m ceiling.

q: Under PD 1096, what occupant-load factor applies to reviewing stands, stadia and waiting spaces?
n: 0.65 sq m per person, the same as an auditorium.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum exit door width applies?
n: 900 mm wide by 2.00 m high.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum open space applies to a corner lot with E, F, G, H or I occupancy?
n: 5%, half the 10% required of A, B, C, D and J occupancies.

q: What occupant-load factor applies to business occupancy?
n: 9.30 sq m per person, the office figure.

q: Under BP 220, what residential open space applies to a through lot?
n: 10% residential, 15% for other uses.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum area and least dimension must a toilet and bath have?
n: 1.20 sq m with a least dimension of 0.90 m, the smallest room the Code allows.

q: Under PD 1096, what minimum ceiling height applies to a habitable room with natural ventilation?
n: 2.70 m with natural ventilation, against 2.40 m with artificial.

q: Under BP 220, what open space applies to a corner lot abutting three or more streets or rivers?
n: 5% for all group occupancies, the lowest figure BP 220 sets.

q: What minimum area must the outside window of a sleeping room have?
n: 0.45 sq m, with a least dimension of 56 cm.

q: Under RA 9514, how must a threshold be treated once its rise exceeds 6 mm?
n: It must be bevelled at a 1:2 slope. Under 6 mm it may be left square.
